findings.desc: Auth bundle paths are not allowlisted before being mounted into Docker. run-probe.mjs only checks fs.existsSync on CELL06_ACCOUNT_*_AUTH_BUNDLE, then passes that unchecked value to docker -v and later records hostHomeMounted=false/repoMounted=false/latticeMounted=false. A user can point the env var at /Users/jek, ~/.codex, this repo, .lattice, or another contaminated host path and still get receipts that claim sterile mounts because validate-probe only checks receipt strings, not the actual env-supplied mount source. This violates CHK-001 adversarial sterile-mount proof and can leak host Codex config or repo material into the container.

Concept blocker: the sterile runner lets arbitrary CELL06_ACCOUNT_*_AUTH_BUNDLE paths be mounted into Docker without an allowlist or host-neutral classification. detectAccounts only checks fs.existsSync, maybeRunCodexExec passes that unchecked value to docker -v, and the receipts still assert hostHomeMounted=false, repoMounted=false, latticeMounted=false, and paperMounted=false. validate-probe verifies only the recorded booleans/env labels, not the actual auth source. A bundle env var can point at /Users/jek, ~/.codex, this repo, .lattice, or paper material and still produce a sterile local-docker receipt, violating the CHK-001/CHK-003 adversarial isolation boundary.
